extracted.intended_audience: general public; social reformers; readers interested in urban poverty and tenement conditions
extracted.subtask_description: A late-19th-century social-reporting chapter describing living conditions, health hazards, and social dynamics in New York tenements and immigrant neighborhoods. It documents physical, sanitary, and social factors that mark slum severity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to sunlight and ventilation
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether rooms and yards receive direct sunlight and have adequate ventilation (e.g., Roosevelt Street alley 'with a five-story house on one side that gets its light and air...from this slit between brick walls' and 'the rays of the sun...never do').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lack of sunlight and air is linked to higher mortality (an English doctor's experiment showed mortality 'one hundred per cent. greater' on the side shut off from the sun). Assess by presence/absence of windows, blind walls, and narrow slits that prevent sun and fresh air from reaching living spaces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fire safety and accessibility of fire-escapes
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether fire-escapes and exits are present and actually reachable in an emergency ('There were fire-escapes, yes! but so placed that they could not be reached').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate placement and obstruction of fire-escapes, clarity of thoroughfares, and whether occupants could realistically use escapes; failures are shown by deadly fires that 'burned up women and children' because escapes or thoroughfares were inaccessible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanitation of common facilities (sinks, pumps, hallways)
rubrics_metrics.description: The state and placement of shared sanitary fixtures and their effect on health (e.g., 'The sinks are in the hallway, that all the tenants may have access--and all be poisoned alike by their summer stenches.' 'Hear the pump squeak!').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect location and cleanliness of sinks, pumps, and shared tubs; assess whether shared facilities concentrate filth and create summer stenches that poison whole blocks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overcrowding / occupancy density
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of people sharing rooms and the resulting crowding (examples: nine people in two rooms; 'Six grown people and five children'; 'one hundred thousand people lived in rear tenements').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure persons per room, multi-use of single rooms (parlor/bedroom/kitchen), and sleeping arrangements (beds, boxes, cradles). Overcrowding correlates with disease, high mortality, and degrading living conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affordability and rent burden relative to wages
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether rent is disproportionately high compared to earnings (example: rent 'seven dollars and a half a month, more than a week's wages for the husband').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare rent to typical weekly/monthly wages of occupants; high rent burdens force extreme crowding and poor living choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structural habitability and condemnation status
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether buildings are condemned or otherwise declared 'unfit for human beings to live in' and whether owners comply with health orders ('their army of tenants was turned out by the health officers because the houses had been condemned').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check official condemnation records, health officers' orders, and whether owners repair properties; condemnation is a formal indicator of uninhabitable conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infant and child mortality as sanitary barometer
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of child and infant death-rates as an indicator of overall sanitary condition ('The infant mortality...is justly considered a good barometer of its general sanitary condition').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess death-rates (under-five and infant deaths) and compare with city averages; the chapter provides detailed local statistics (e.g., block death-rates and totals) showing far higher child mortality in worst tenement blocks than the city average.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presence and effect of nearby refuse/dumps and rag-picking settlements
rubrics_metrics.description: Proximity to ash-barrels, dumps, and rag-pickers' settlements that contaminate living areas and are tied to economic exploitation ('the ash-barrels...form the staples of their trade' and rag-picker settlements sleeping/working amid 'unutterable horror').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether tenants live adjacent to or within dump sites, whether refuse is used as market counters, and how dump settlements affect sanitation and health; note municipal contracts that institutionalize the exploitation of such sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and functionality of basic household equipment (stove, boiler, water)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether households have proper stoves, boilers, and safe cooking/washing arrangements (e.g., 'The family tea-kettle is on the stove, doing duty...as a wash-boiler' and leaking stove pipes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect condition of stoves, pipes, and multi-use of limited appliances that create smoke, fumes, or unsafe conditions; broken or improvised equipment worsens health and fire risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cleanliness and capacity for personal hygiene
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability of families to keep clothes and persons clean ('It is washday all the week round...a change of clothing is scarce among the poor' and 'the true line to be drawn between pauperism and honest poverty is the clothes-line').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess frequency and possibility of laundering, availability of clean clothing, and overcrowded washing facilities; chronic uncleanliness reflects poverty and limited means rather than moral failing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Landlord responsibility and enforcement of repairs
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether landlords are held to account and make repairs (examples of landlords wealthy and influential yet owning condemned property; 'the owner...will oppose every order to put his property in repair').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review tax and ownership records, health department orders, and landlords' responses; effective enforcement and making owners repair property is necessary to improve conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Occupational and economic exploitation of immigrant labor (padrone system)
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which immigrants (especially Italians) are subject to exploitative middlemen—steamship agents, 'bankers', padrones—who mortgage wages, extract commissions, and control access to jobs and housing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine presence of padrone-mediated contracts, mortgages on immigrant wages and belongings, exclusive control of work (e.g., ash-scows), and how these arrangements limit immigrants' independence and worsen poverty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language, education, and capacity for self-advocacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether immigrant groups can speak/read English and thus avoid exploitation ('He not only knows no word of English, but he does not know enough to learn'), affecting their ability to access fair employment and defend rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess literacy and English-language uptake among immigrant families; language barriers correlate with dependence on middlemen and vulnerability to fraud and extortion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Street-level public life versus adequate private space
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree to which daily life and economic activity are forced into streets/sidewalks due to lack of private space ('When the sun shines the entire population seeks the street, carrying on its household work, its bargaining, its love-making on street or sidewalk').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe whether households conduct food preparation, trade, and social life in public spaces because interiors are too small or uninhabitable; this indicates deficient housing stock and contributes to public health nuisances.
